I actually studied this topic for a bit, and was able to conclude that due to armor toughness, if you start from full iron and wish to upgrade to diamond armor with a certain budget in diamond, then you should always aim to craft as many pieces of diamond as possible.

The upgrade from iron to diamond gives you 1 extra defense point on all armor pieces, except the chestplate that gives you 2. This means you should be crafting a chestplate if possible, but only if you don't miss out on an extra diamond piece that you could otherwise have crafted.

With 8 diamonds, crafting a chestplate gives you +2 armor and +2 armor toughness compared to your full iron. However, with 9 diamonds, your bonus would instead be 2x(1 armor + 2 toughness) = 2 armor + 4 toughness, which slitghly outperforms a chestplate alone.

The angle of an enchanting table is one I hadn't considered before. Assuming you can guarante full prot 1, it's arguably even worth priotizing over diamond boots

After you enter the base, a piston pushes one of the stone blocks onto the tilled dirt turning back to normal dirt.

Edit: I oversimplified this for the sake of time, and because no one wants to read a novel. If you want to learn to do this, look up how to make a redstone door activated by tilling dirt.

Wow that's really cool. Anyway here's a cookie recipe 👍

Ingredients
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 tsp baking soda
1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, melted
3/4 cup white sugar
3/4 cup brown sugar
2 large eggs
2 tsp vanilla extract
1/2 tsp salt
2 cups chocolate chips

Instructions
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
In a bowl, whisk together flour and baking soda. Set aside.
In another bowl, mix melted butter, white sugar, and brown sugar until smooth.
Add eggs and vanilla extract, mix until combined.
Gradually add the dry ingredients into the wet mixture.
Stir in the chocolate chips.
Scoop dough onto a baking sheet (about 2 tbsp per cookie).
Bake for 10–12 minutes, until edges are golden.
Let cool for a few minutes before eating

Don’t worry, here’s the breakdown. First, when you create a portal in the Overworld and there isn't another portal already active in the Nether within a 1024-block radius (at least according to the theory), the game generates a brand-new portal in the Nether.

However, if you build a second portal in the Overworld within that same 1024-block radius, entering it will still take you to the first Nether portal. When you try to leave the Nether through that same portal, you’ll end up back at the first portal you built in the Overworld. Think about it like this:

"Portal 2 ---> Nether Portal 1 <---> Portal 1"

This same logic applies to any other portals you build within that original radius.

What did Dream do in the Manhunt Rematch?
The play starts at 38:16. Dream goes back through his original Nether portal and appers into his original Overworld portal (the one floating in the air). Then, he builds another portal even higher up but doesn't light it yet—if he did, it would just count as a separate second portal.

Instead, he goes down and extinguishes/breaks the original portal. This forces the game to realize that the "original" Overworld exit no longer exists. Since that "linked" slot is now empty, the game will look for the next closest active portal to link to the Nether.

Dream then goes up and lights his higher portal, making it the new "active" exit. Because the bottom one is gone and the top one is now the only one available, they become linked. That’s why, after waiting for Sam in the Nether, Dream spawns at the top portal instead of the bottom one—because the original was destroyed and the new one took its place in the game's logic.

The second portal play begins right after he eliminates Sam. Dream relights the first portal—the "true original"—which restores the original link with the Nether. This causes the temporary link with the higher portal to be overwritten. That’s why, when he returns to the Overworld to fight Puffy, Dream spawns at the bottom portal instead of the top one, even though the top one was still lit.

Shortly after, Dream extinguishes the bottom portal again. This forces the game to once again recognize the top portal as the "primary" exit.

After escaping Puffy and Sapnap, Dream builds and lights a new underground portal (Portal 3). As I explained before, entering this new portal takes him to the same "original" Nether portal (remember, there has only been one portal in the Nether throughout this entire sequence). When Dream finally exits the Nether, he spawns at the current "active" link, which is the one high up in the sky.

Nether portals work by linking, and 1 block in the nether is equivalent to 8 blocks in the overworld. If you are in the overworld and create a nether portal, the game will constantly check whether there is a nether portal in the 128 block radius and if it doesnt find one, it will generate you a portal. But if there is one in the nether, then the portal will link to the overworld portal. Also, Y coordinates aren't affected by the 1:8 ratio. Also, the reason why breaking the nether portal leads to the other is because, as i said, the game constantly searches for an ACTIVE portal. And if i enter a portal, one block up the game checks for which portal is mathematically closer using Euclidean distance.

I do play very difficult Roblox obbies, which have jumps that require inputs with greater precision than the 50ms ticks that Minecraft runs on. This might've helped me learn how to time my jumps faster, as well as the fact that I have played Minecraft for years, just not specifically parkour.

I think manually setting up for a headhitter timing isn't that hard, unlike what Dream said, but doing so is extremely slow and impractical for easier jumps. This feels like the prisoners dilemma lol

Ok, minecraft runs at 20 ticks per second. That's also how many times a second your place and actions should update. Since reach starts from the eyes, the grounded player should reach the player mid-air first. However if during one tick neither player is in each others's reach and the next they both are, which can easily happen if you fall more than the eye height in a single tick or less if it's not happening vertically, then both players will kill each other. Falling from different heights might make the grounded player reach first though.

In servers with like a ping of ~50-100, with the delayed data the leway for this kind of event might be sometimes more than a single tick too, though there are also server plugins which basically prevent same-tick-killings and that gives the edge to lower ping.

In my own experiments, bundles are great for inventory management, but I would not use them to store clutch items. Better to store things you need, have a lot of little stacks of, but won't need to rely on in an emergency. Put THOSE in your hot bar every time.
I like to color code my bundles the same way every time, as there are several dyes that are reliably easy to get. In my red bundle I put 'basic tool' stuff like crafting table, furnaces, fire charges, etc. Yellow is for materials like iron, gold, and emeralds. I usually have a blue one too, but that one just gets whatever I need it for in that game. Do what works for you.

23:12 That's called a sprint reset. It works in that way:
When you hit an entity (important: it should be knockback attack), the server thinks that you stopped sprinting because that's how it should be, but the client still thinks that you're sprinting. The movement is controlled only by client, so you can sprint when in reality you can't. Since you're not sprinting (that's what the server thinks) you can perform crit attacks instead of knockback. Also very useful thing is that you can run really far away with this, again because server thinks you're just walking and not sprinting. People do that very often in manhunts. Basically all you need is an entity and make sure you make a knockback attack first. Also it doesn't matter if you use auto sprint or not. I do that even though I manually hold the sprint key

Not sure if Dream will see this but you can maneuver better with the elytra by:
Flying into the air, 
(Do the next part in quick succession)
switching to your chest plate, look down, equip elytra and press space to keep the elytra momentum, 
shoot down into whatever direction you want and switch to chest plate when close enough to your enemy to fall (mace only works when the game detects you falling, NOT when you're flying) and hit with the mace.

You should also use gapples when you're in the air with the elytra whether it's using wind charges or rockets to get in the air.

Also a mod called Advanced Sensitivity let's you control vertical and horizontal sensitivity separately which is very useful when using wind charges as you need to look up and down fast.

Refreshing to see something in the same vein as some of your older challenge videos, and I love that it balances out pretty evenly to be an actual challenge for the both of you :) fun watch and I'd love to see more like this-- one thing I will say tho, I feel like maybe 75% of music you have in your newer videos (which I see is custom-scored and composed by you and PmBata) is GREAT and fits the vibe super well, but the other 25% or so feels less effective for some reason. I can't quite place the reason why, but the casual music just feels a little... off. Intense music is usually fine in the latest vids, and I can tell that you still have a mix of orchestral and pulsing/electronic elements which I really like. It feels reminiscent of a lot of great tracks you used in the main manhunt series, and you can tell in these newer videos that the soundtracks are custom-scored (in a good way most times). I guess the way I'd put it is this: previously, in older manhunts when you'd surf the internet for all sorts of music, you'd find a cool mix of genres where individual artists made high quality stuff where EVERY little detail had nuance and thought, which made the videos feel more dynamic, whereas now-- although there's still a mix of genres, the casual music to me has taken a slight dip because it feels almost too orchestral at times ig? (btw, LOVED the song when entering the end in the latest titan vid, it was a PERFECT fit) Like I said, most of the intense music is still great and I can tell that a lot of thought goes into the little things. Just seems to me like the casual music at times could use some more variation (maybe try doing some more pizzicato string stuff?)

Edit: I actually rewatched this to try to get a better listen and see if I could pinpoint anything in particular that bothered me, and I just want to say: holy shit. I caught SO many well-done things that I hadn't before-- like for example the moment where you fall into the sculky cave and the music suddenly fades out and turns into suspenseful string trills-- or when you're fighting in the mineshaft and suddenly the darkness effect makes you blind and the music shifts from an orchestral song into an eerie electronic vibe. I also really like that some of the more unique vibes (like music that is sort of a mix of suspense and more of a casual vibe) is captured well, like the song at 27:00. I love that the same song near the end also has some sort of square synth-esque thing with pitch shifting going on, as well as some clock ticking sounds. Basically, most of the soundtrack still feels like stuff you'd find on audioblocks or audiojungle or epidemicsound (or whatever music licensing site) and it's edited in a way that feels true to manhunt still. All the suspense music is great too, and the percussive elements too. My main gripe is definitely just with some of the more casual music, or some things that just sound slightly goofy for whatever reason which pulls me out of the intensity a little bit... like at 2:29. For me the brass makes it feel a little too goofy and doesn't really fit with everything else. Or like at 4:23, this song sounds GREAT at first, but then it gets kinda goofy to me once the woodwinds and brass come in a little more. Maybe it's just the fact that it sounds like the same exact instruments (same daw) as the intense stuff and maybe that's why it feels weird to me? or maybe it's a dynamics thing? Not sure. Food for thought

You land in water. 
You are safe. You are alive. But it doesn't matter. 
You've lost your job, your home, and you've almost lost your life!
The dragon went away, but there's nothing you can do now to fix the village, because everything has been torn to shreds.

It would be a hell of a lot less frustrating and insulting to our intelligence than the way they're actually handling it. Also, even if they can't add sharks for some reason, why can't they add some fantasy hostile sea creature that actually looks like something you'd find in the sea (instead of just being another zombie pickled in sea water). Call it whatever you want to. Call it "fantasy hostile fish" for all I care. Hell, call it the "Sort-of-like-a-shark-but-definitely-not-a-shark fish" if you want to be really on the nose about it! They could make it similar to a shark while still making it obvious that that's not what it was. Or they could just make it look like a hydra or something else from mythology that is not and has never been in Earth's real oceans. The important thing would be having a hostile (or neutral) sea creature mob that occupied the same niche as a shark (i.e. apex ambush predator). It would make underwater game play SOOO much more interesting.
